Help.Title: User guide
Help.Subtitle: Build PS5 FPKG packages, pack PS4 PKGs, move files over FTP and resign saves — on macOS, Windows and Linux
Help.Quick.Title: Quick start — PS5 FPKG
Help.Quick.1: Prepare the extracted PS5 app folder: it must contain a sce_sys folder (param.json, icon0.png…) and eboot.bin. You can also pick a GP5 project (.gp5) from Publishing Tools / fpkg-gui — the package then contains exactly the files the project lists.
Help.Quick.2: In step 1 click Game folder… or drop the folder onto the window. Content ID, title, version, size and junk files are detected automatically.
Help.Quick.3: Choose the output folder for the .pkg. The temp folder is suggested on the same volume to avoid cross-volume copies, and free space is checked for you.
Help.Quick.4: Pick a speed preset in step 3 (Fast · Standard · Smallest · Maximum). Standard (level 4) is the default: it is the same encoder the 2.0.0 engine used for its Kraken 7, so you get the old size at the old speed. Smallest (level 7, Optimal) is about 3 % smaller but 5–6× slower. Or open the advanced options.
Help.Quick.5: Click Build PKG (Ctrl/⌘+B or F5). Watch the progress, remaining time and log; when finished the package structure is verified and the result is shown.
Help.Speed.Title: Speed & optimisation
Help.Speed.1: • The built-in Kraken encoder uses every CPU core; threads = 0 means automatic. On Windows, native Oodle is preferred when libScePubTools.dll is present.
Help.Speed.2: • The default preset is Standard (Kraken level 4) — in the 2.0.0 engine levels 4–7 all used this Normal encoder, so it reproduces the old "Kraken 7" result at the old speed. Smallest (level 7, Optimal3) shrinks the package by roughly 3 % more but takes 5–6× longer on real game data; Fast (level 2) is for quick tests. Already-compressed files (video, audio, textures) are stored raw automatically.
Help.Speed.3: • Uncompressed mode builds about twice as fast but produces a noticeably larger package — handy for quick tests.
Help.Speed.4: • Put the temp folder on an SSD, on the same volume as the output. You need roughly 1.1× the source size free for the temp image and 1.1× for the .pkg.
Help.Speed.5: • The app keeps the computer awake while building (caffeinate on macOS, SetThreadExecutionState on Windows) — disable it in the advanced options if you prefer.
Help.Speed.6: • Post-build SHA-256 re-reads the entire .pkg; for packages of tens of GB enable it only when needed.
Help.Notes.Title: Important notes
Help.Notes.1: • The output and temp folders must not be inside the source folder.
Help.Notes.2: • The result is a debug FPKG (FIH, signed byte 0x00) — it only installs on a PS5 with debug mode enabled.
Help.Notes.3: • On macOS, Finder creates .DS_Store files; the app detects them and offers to remove them so they do not end up in the package.
Help.Notes.4: • The passcode defaults to 32 zeros — only change it when you really need to.
Help.Notes.5: • Enable deterministic builds to reproduce an identical package from the same source.
Help.Notes.6: • Use the fpkg-cli command-line tool for batch or automated builds (see README).

Help.About.Body: PSVIETHOA FPKG Builder is a cross-platform (macOS, Windows & Linux) application written in C# / .NET with Avalonia UI, developed by PSVIETHOA (Nguyễn Thanh Sơn & Ngô Phi Phương) on top of Drakmor's LibProsperoPkg 1.2.0 library: debug FPKG creation, PlayGo, Kraken/Oodle compression, SDK override and result verification. Since 3.0.0 it also packs PS4 PKGs (orbis-pub-cmd 3.87 + LibOrbisPkg), transfers files to the PS5 over FTP and resigns PS4/PS5 saves — ported from PSVIETHOA STUDIO by Ngô Phi Phương.

Cli.Help:
PSVIETHOA FPKG Builder CLI — build PS5 FPKG (FIH debug) and PS4 PKG packages.

USAGE
  fpkg-cli build --source <dir> --output <dir> [options]
  fpkg-cli inspect <source dir|.exfat|.ffpfsc|.ffpkg|.gp5> [--output <dir>]
  fpkg-cli verify <file.pkg> [--sha256] [--full] [--passcode X]
  fpkg-cli clean-junk <dir> [--dry-run]
  fpkg-cli info
  fpkg-cli check-update
  fpkg-cli install-dokan                (Windows) install the bundled Dokan driver for copy-free mounting
  fpkg-cli dlc-from-ini <folder|image|dlc_emu.ini> --output <dir> [--image plaintext|native]   build one DLC package per entry of dlc_emu.ini (default PLAINTEXT_NOAUTH, like game packages)
  fpkg-cli pkg-info <file.pkg> [--passcode X] [--sha256]
  fpkg-cli pkg-list <file.pkg> [--include <glob>]...
  fpkg-cli pkg-extract <file.pkg> --output <dir> [--include <glob>]... [--cnt] [--no-sce-sys] [--passcode X] [--threads N] [--temp <dir>]
  fpkg-cli pkg-dlc-template <file.pkg> [--output <dir>] [--passcode X]

OPTIONS for build
  -s, --source <dir|.exfat|.ffpkg|.gp5> App folder (contains sce_sys/), an exFAT/.ffpfsc/.ffpkg image, or a GP5 project.
  -o, --output <dir>       Output folder for the .pkg.
      --temp <dir>         Temporary folder (default: same volume as the output).
  -c, --content-id <id>    36-character Content ID (default: read from sce_sys/param.json).
  -t, --title <name>       App title (when param.json has none).
  -v, --version <NN.NNN.NNN>
      --kind app|homebrew|dlc          Package type (default app).
      --image plaintext|native        Outer image mode (default plaintext).
      --preset fast|balanced|smallest|maximum  Speed/compression preset (default balanced = Standard: level 4, the old engine's "Kraken 7"; aliases sony|standard; smallest = level 7 Optimal, slow).
      --backend auto|builtin|pubtools|none
      --level <-4..9>      Kraken level (default 4).
      --threads <n>        Compression threads (0 = every core). Sony SDK: limits img_create to n cores.
      --playgo <1..800>    Fallback PlayGo chunks (default 100; Sony SDK 1..800, built-in engine 1..255; a source playgo-chunk.dat supplies the count).
      --sdk <1..11>        Override the SDK major version (Sony SDK: writes sdkVersion into param.json like the fix15 toolkit's --sdk-version; must match eboot.bin).
      --passcode <32 chars>
      --dll <path>         libScePubTools.dll (Windows only).
      --sha256             Compute SHA-256 after building.
      --full-verify        Decrypt and test-decompress every file after building (the quick content check always runs).
      --no-deterministic   Disable deterministic builds.
      --clean-junk         Delete .DS_Store/Thumbs.db… from the source first.
      --no-sleep-guard     Do not keep the computer awake.
      --quiet              Print only progress and the result.
      --exfat auto|mount|extract   .exfat/.ffpfsc images: copy-free mount (hdiutil on macOS, Dokan on Windows) or extract to the temp folder (default auto).
      --pfs v2|v3          PFS compression format (default v2; v3 unlocks shuffles/region hints).
      --block-size <KiB>   Kraken block size 128..256 (default 256).
      --shuffle <pattern>  PFS v3 shuffle: none, PredictForStructs, PredictForBc1..5, Shuffle116, …
      --shuffle-analysis   Automatic shuffle analysis (PFS v3).
      --shuffle-prediction-level <-4..9|auto>
      --skip-pfs-input-check   Skip the PFS v3 input compatibility check (expert).
      --no-sony-sdk        Build with the built-in engine instead of the Sony SDK (default: Sony SDK — Publishing Tools 2.79, needs a 96-byte sce_sys/keystone; runs through the bundled Wine on macOS).
      --no-sdk-prescan     Sony SDK on Windows: skip the parallel pre-scan of source files (default: on; Windows Defender scans each file on first open and Publishing Tools checks files one by one).
      --sdk-compression-level <-4..9>   Sony SDK: pass --compression_level to Publishing Tools (default: not passed = level 7 like the original toolkit; lower = faster, larger package).
      --no-sdk-playgo-fallback   Sony SDK: do NOT use the PlayGo fallback (on by default): when the source has no sce_sys/playgo-chunk.dat, create 1 chunk / 1 scenario like the old script instead of --playgo chunks (default 100) with one chunk per language like the toolkit.
      --sdk-drop-empty-folders     Sony SDK: do NOT keep the source's empty folders (kept by default as <empty_dir> GP5 entries, like the built-in engine); dlc_emu.ini mount folders are still kept.
      --sdk-keep-empty-chunks      Sony SDK: leave PlayGo chunks that have no files empty, like the toolkit (default: each gets an uncompressed 1 MiB placeholder, because the PS5 treats an empty chunk as not installed and a game that waits for it stops at “Installing game 0GB/0”).
      --sdk-retail-scenarios       Sony SDK: when the source still has a valid PlayGo table, keep the retail scenarios' chunk order and initial chunk count like the fix15 toolkit (default: every scenario lists every chunk, every chunk initial — avoids the CE-108111-2 error seen with Ghost of Yōtei).
      --sdk-reference <base.pkg>   Sony SDK: build an UPDATE against this base package (img_create --ref_pkg_path). The source may be the full new game or an update folder with only changed/added files; files it lacks come from the base package. Writes UPDATE_<id>….pkg and <id>….remastered.pkg. Use --version to raise the content version.
      --sdk-base-folder <dir>      Update: read the files the source lacks from the original game folder instead of extracting them from the base package (read only).
      --sdk-patch-output update|full|both   Update: keep only UPDATE_….pkg, only the full ….remastered.pkg, or both (default).
      --sdk-patch-exact            Update: treat the source as the complete new version (missing files = deleted), like the toolkit.
      --sdk-build-base             With --sdk-base-folder and no --sdk-reference: build the base package from the original game folder first, then the update against it.
      --sdk-keep-intermediate      Sony SDK: keep the generated .gp5, scenario file and .gp5-assets next to the package.
      --keep-drm           Keep applicationDrmType as in the source (default: forced to "standard").
      --keep-ampr          Keep the AMPR emu leftovers (ampr_emu.index) in the package.
      --keep-dump-leftovers  Keep dump leftovers (_DUBLEX_, Unreal Engine/Saved and <project>/Saved folders) in the package.
      --keep-playgo        Keep the source's sce_sys/playgo* files (the default since 2.2.6; the engine keeps their chunk layout).
      --remove-playgo      Drop the source's sce_sys/playgo* files; the engine generates a fresh layout.

Help.Notes.7: • A source can be an exFAT disk image (.exfat) or a .ffpfsc container (the PFSC-compressed exFAT image some dump tools produce). On macOS the app mounts .exfat images with hdiutil and builds directly (no copy); on Windows click "Enable direct mounting" in the advanced options (the Dokan driver is bundled, one administrator prompt) to mount the same way — a read-only virtual drive served by the app that also handles .ffpfsc, hides junk files and applies the DRM fix on the drive. When mounting is impossible (no Dokan, .ffpfsc on macOS, junk files on macOS) the app extracts the image to the temp folder and cleans up afterwards. A GP5 project (.gp5) is read exactly as written — Normal layout (rootdir + exclude masks) or Flat layout (explicit file list); relative paths resolve from the folder containing the .gp5, and the output / temp folders must be outside both the project root and the folder holding the .gp5 (the output folder is suggested right next to it).
Help.Notes.8: • PFS v3 + automatic shuffle analysis optimises texture compression through a permutation-selection pass: it is very time-consuming and only fully effective at Kraken level 9 (the Maximum preset). PFS v3 packages need PS5 firmware 7.00 or newer — on older firmware the game may not launch, so keep PFS v2 unless you need the extra savings.
Help.Notes.9: • Every time it starts, the app checks GitHub Releases (can be turned off in the advanced options). When a newer version exists the header shows a green badge, the ↻ button gets a dot and a dialog asks whether to download it; the ↻ button checks manually at any time. Nothing is ever downloaded automatically.

Rosetta.Title: Install Rosetta 2?
Rosetta.Body:
The Sony SDK is a Windows x86-64 program that runs through the bundled Wine, which needs Apple's Rosetta 2 on Apple Silicon. macOS removes Rosetta after some major upgrades (for example to macOS 27).

The app will run Apple's own installer:
softwareupdate --install-rosetta --agree-to-license

By continuing you accept Apple's Rosetta licence. It needs an internet connection and takes about a minute; no administrator password is required.
Rosetta.Done: Rosetta 2 is installed — the Sony SDK build method is available again.

Page.Ps5Build.Description: Build an FPKG (FIH debug) from an app folder, an .exfat / .ffpfsc / .ffpkg image or a .gp5 project — Sony SDK or the built-in engine; a package is only reported as done after it has been verified.
Page.Ps5Update.Description: Pick the base package installed on the console; the source is the full new game or just a folder with the changed files. The Sony SDK writes UPDATE_….pkg (delta) and/or the full package.
Page.Ps5Extract.Description: Open a PS5 PKG to see its details, verify its structure and extract everything or individual files.
Page.Ps5Queue.Description: Drop many game folders, disk images or a whole dump drive into the queue; each entry uses the Build PKG settings at the moment it starts.
Page.Ps4Extract.Description: Extract a PS4 FPKG into its own folder (image0 + manifest): everything or only the files you pick. The source package is only read.
Page.Ps4Base.Description: Build a PS4 game folder into a base PKG with the Fake PKG Tools 3.87 publishing engine; the GP4 is generated automatically.
Page.Ps4Patch.Description: Build a PS4 update that installs over the base — a patch or a translation — and edit param.sfo on a copy; a base locked with another passcode still works.
Page.Ps4Dlc.Description: Rebuild a DLC with data after editing files in image0; the Content ID, version and entitlement key stay as in the original package.
Page.Ps4Merge.Description: Merge a base and an update into one base PKG that holds the update data and installs once. Each source is a PKG or an extracted folder.
Page.Ftp.Description: Browse and transfer files between this computer and the PS5 through ftpsrv (port 2121): multi-thread upload and download, new folders, rename, delete.
Page.SaveResign.Description: Re-own PS4 / PS5 saves to your Account ID and install them straight onto the console through garlic-savemgr. The source save files are only read.

Help.Ps4.Title: PS4 PKG
Help.Ps4.1: • Five modes: Extract PKG, Build base, Build update, Build DLC and Merge base + update. Pick or drag in the source (.pkg or game folder): the right-hand card previews its icon, title, Content ID, Title ID and version.
Help.Ps4.2: • Packages are built with orbis-pub-cmd 3.87 (CyB1K patch) and LibOrbisPkg, following the PSVIETHOA STUDIO workflow: a GP4 project, PFS compression and the source PlayGo layout. The fast engine is the default; turn on Full mode to use the original engine with full digests.
Help.Ps4.3: • The param.sfo tab edits the title (every language), version and other fields before packing; the edited copy is saved separately and the source stays untouched.
Help.Ps4.4: • macOS and Linux run orbis-pub-cmd through Wine (32-bit support needed; the macOS app bundles it). Windows needs the VC++ 2008 SP1 x86 and VC++ 2015–2022 x86 runtimes; the app installs them when missing.
Help.Ftp.Title: PS5 FTP
Help.Ftp.1: • Start an FTP server on the PS5 (usually port 2121), enter its IP and Connect. Leave User and Password empty unless the server asks for them; the password is never saved.
Help.Ftp.2: • Drag files between the Computer and PS5 panes, drag from Finder/Explorer into the PS5 pane to upload, or drop onto a folder to send straight into it. Drag PS5 files onto another PS5 folder to move them.
Help.Ftp.3: • The queue picks how many files run in parallel, splits large files over several connections and resumes after a drop. Keys: Enter opens/transfers, Delete deletes, F2 renames, F5 refreshes, Backspace goes up.
Help.Save.Title: Save resign
Help.Save.1: • Decrypted saves (a folder, param.sfo or .zip) are resigned right on the computer: the app changes ACCOUNT_ID (and TITLE_ID when given) and keeps a .bak of the original param.sfo; a .zip gets a new _resigned.zip copy.
Help.Save.2: • Encrypted saves (PS5 sdimg_…, PS4 save image + .bin) need the PS5 running garlic-savemgr (port 8082). Press Load ELF to send the bundled garlic-savemgr to the ELF loader (port 9021), then Scan users to fetch the Account ID.
Help.Save.3: • Before overwriting a save on the console, the app downloads a backup into its data folder (save-backups).

Zstd.Ui.PreviewIntro.Pack:
ZSTD pack (ps5-dump-forge format, ampr-emu-ng runtime):

  ampr_zstd.index          file table (AMPRZPK1)
  ampr_zstd-000.pak …      data, each file < 4 GiB
  fakelib/libSceAmpr.sprx  ampr-emu-ng 0.3.4
  ampr_emu.index           table of every file (AMPRIDX3)

Every file is cut into 256 KiB chunks, one ZSTD frame each (chunks that do not shrink stay raw). Left loose: eboot.bin, *.prx, *.sprx, *.elf, *.self, *.ini, sce_sys/, sce_module/, fakelib*/.

The original game folder is NOT modified: the result goes to a new folder; then build a PKG from it on the Build PKG page like any game folder.
Zstd.Ui.PreviewIntro.Unpack: ZSTD unpack: every packed file is decoded byte-exact (ZSTD frames carry a checksum), loose files are copied; ampr_emu.index is rewritten from the real sizes and the runtime goes back to the original ampr_emu 0.4.2.1 (unless you keep it).
